documentation_citations.quote_summary: Defect D-c, 'Per-game execution scope': daily_forecast.py cannot be scoped to one game and keys deduplication on now; severity A for confirmation validity; cross-thread amendment bundled with the forecast_log.py schema change.
Appendix F contract-amendment map: daily_forecast.py -- 'per-game scope; stop keying deduplication on now (D-c)', owner engineering, bundle yes.
D-c is item (i) of a four-fault repair set; D-b, D-a, D-d are separate.
D-b / D-c / D-f mean served obligations are not a random subset, which must be accounted for whenever the period is graded.
Decision D-4: the bundled cross-thread amendment is 'Prepare, do not implement.'
prospective_v0 uses two fixed daily runs; 'Per-game dispatching is a documented v1 upgrade' -- i.e. the absence of per-game scope is contractually expected in v0, not an accident.

limb_1_no_per_game_scope.measured: In forecasts/forecast_log.jsonl no firing ever produced fewer than 2 records (records_per_cutoff_min = 2, max = 3); in experiments/forecast_dryrun/scratch_chain.jsonl every firing produced exactly 3 (min = max = 3). No single-game execution exists anywhere in either chain.

evidence: daily_forecast.py:893-895 -- 'now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)'; 'cutoff = ... if args.cutoff else now'.
evalharness/forecast_log.py:697-707 -- the duplicate key is (game_id, forecast_cutoff, model_version_hash).

Measured: 0 of 3 distinct forecast_cutoff values in the official chain and 1 of 5 in the scratch chain fall on a round second. Every scheduled cutoff carries microsecond resolution, i.e. it is a wall clock, so the key can never collide.

measured.note: Records 0-2 and 6-8 of the scratch chain are the same three games at the same three labels under the same model_version_hash, logged by two firings 110 seconds apart. The chain accepted all six. The shipped duplicate refusal fired zero times in the entire history of both chains.

limb_2_dedup_keyed_on_now.synthetic_reproduction: TESTS.py test 1: four simulated 15-minute firings at the T-30m obligation produce four chain records and zero DuplicateForecastError refusals, all four carrying one obligation identity, with the hash chain still verifying. The defect is semantic, not an integrity failure.

additional_finding_not_in_the_documented.title: decision_time_label is assigned by the firing instant, with no proximity bound
evidence: daily_forecast.py:598-599 -- nearest_label() returns the CONTRACT_LABELS entry minimising |hours_to_tip - label_hours|, with no maximum distance.

Measured on real bytes: game 1022600212 in experiments/forecast_dryrun/scratch_chain.jsonl is recorded as serving T-8h at hours_to_tip 4.806 and 4.776, then T-90m at 4.716. The label flips at the 4.75h midpoint between the 8h and 1.5h contract times.
TESTS.py test 8 reproduces the flip and confirms every real label in that game equals nearest_label(hours_to_tip).
additional_finding_not_in_the_documented.why_it_matters: decision_time_label today records which contract time happened to be nearest to when the job fired, not which obligation the run was dispatched to serve. A record can claim to have served the T-90m obligation from 4.7 hours before tip. This is the mechanism behind the documented 'serves a non-random subset' claim, and it is a precondition for any obligation-keyed fix: the label must become an input (the obligation being served) rather than an output of the wall clock.

fix.kind: call-site wrapper; no shared artifact edited
design: Obligation identity is (game_id, decision_time_label, model_version_hash). Within a game each of the four contract labels occurs exactly once (daily_forecast.py:126), so the triple is complete AND is derivable from schema evalharness/forecast_log/1 records already on disk. No schema change is needed to adopt it.
forecast_cutoff keeps its existing meaning as the as-of data boundary and its existing never-in-the-future refusal (daily_forecast.py:899). The fix does not widen it.

guarded_log_forecast() refuses a repeat serving before delegating to the unmodified evalharness log_forecast, which keeps its own DuplicateForecastError underneath as a second line of defence. The wrapper only ever adds a refusal.

scope_slate_to_games() returns a ScopeDeclaration naming every excluded game, so per-game scope is declared rather than silent and does not violate the COMPLETENESS RULE at daily_forecast.py:1058-1061. game_ids=None reproduces existing whole-slate behaviour byte for byte.
fix.backward_compatibility: Applied to the real official chain the obligation key finds 0 repeat servings, i.e. adopting it would have changed nothing already logged there. Applied to the real scratch chain it finds 3, i.e. it would have refused three repeat servings the shipped key accepted.
fix.not_adopted: The call site in daily_forecast.py is NOT changed by this node. Adoption is a proposal.
